title: Agent platform strategy and roadmap priorities
content:
Danish's strategic direction from 2026-06-08 standup:

Agent Platform role across 3 agent families:
1. Admin agent family - currently strongest role
2. Deals agent family - self-sufficient, early adopters, some net new requirements coming
3. GTM agent family - needs deep support from us (observability, telemetry, alerting, monitoring, UI/UX)

Role: SWAT team - strategically step in, address specific concern, get out. GTM takes priority.

New roadmap elements to introduce:
- Security
- Observability / telemetry
- Toolkit robustness and flexibility for newer integration patterns
- Agent memories not being utilized optimally
- No reinforcement learning happening - agents don't utilize previous conversations

Merger context: renewed focus on AI/agents and pace. Plan B (stay independent) in play while merger is uncertain. Expect more scrutiny on pace and quality.

ai_meta.summary: Danish outlined the Agent Platform's role across three agent families, emphasizing GTM support as the top priority and a SWAT-team operating model. The note also captures new roadmap themes and merger-related context increasing scrutiny on pace and quality.

title: Sprint planning decisions — June 1, 2026
content:
Key decisions and principles from the June 1, 2026 sprint planning:

1. Data table work tracked as a NEW epic — do not reopen the old closed epic. (Lexi to create.)
2. Table controls assumed to take priority over stop-stream unless Himmat says otherwise. (Lexi to confirm with Himmat afternoon of June 1.)
3. Table state reset should NOT be fixed in conversation history immediately if Agent Memory rollout lands within ~1–2 weeks. Plan B needed if rollout slips.
4. Agent Memory rollout path: bug bash → enable in latest → keep in latest ~1 week → production. (Sanket owns.)
5. Copy-paste does not need a fully custom perfect UX; start with AG Grid defaults.
6. No separate row-level copy affordance should be added — manual selection is fine.
7. Duplicate table count display should be streamlined to a single indicator (remove top custom count; keep table-native bottom count).
8. Table title should come from the agent/LLM, not be inferred by the platform.
9. Unified chat component is NOT currently justified as priority work. (Priya to clarify impact.)
10. State management may deserve separate treatment from broad chat unification.
11. Principle: work that is not user-visible or not clearly painful should not automatically be prioritized.
12. Telemetry crew tickets exist, but platform-level span/metric plumbing must be resolved first.
13. New Relic production may require metric whitelisting; latest allows everything.
14. Security enhancements unlikely to be implemented this sprint; design/policy may be ready.
15. Reasoning CS2 should be its own follow-up epic rather than extending CS1 indefinitely.
16. Show-and-tell should be product-style, feature-level demos — not implementation-first technical walkthroughs.
17. Show-and-tell should dissolve frontend/backend boundaries and show complete adoption path (FE, backend contract, memory).
18. HITL may need use cases outside current policy/tool-spec trigger model.
19. Canonical message type estimate is too large; needs a narrower "most gain / least resistance" path. (Danish, Akash, Sanket to sync.)
